sanskrit.deva:
तदेतत्सत्यं यथा सुदीप्तात्पावकाद्विस्फुलिङ्गाः सहस्रशः प्रभवन्ते सरूपाः ।
तथाक्षराद्विविधाः सोम्य भावाः प्रजायन्ते तत्र चैवापियन्ति ॥ १ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
tad etat satyaṃ yathā sudīptāt pāvakād visphuliṅgāḥ sahasraśaḥ prabhavante sarūpāḥ |
tathākṣarād vividhāḥ somya bhāvāḥ prajāyante tatra caivāpiyanti || 1 ||

lines.iast: tad etat satyaṃ yathā sudīptāt pāvakād visphuliṅgāḥ sahasraśaḥ prabhavante sarūpāḥ
lines.deva: तदेतत्सत्यं यथा सुदीप्तात्पावकाद्विस्फुलिङ्गाः सहस्रशः प्रभवन्ते सरूपाः

lines.iast: tathākṣarād vividhāḥ somya bhāvāḥ prajāyante tatra caivāpiyanti
lines.deva: तथाक्षराद्विविधाः सोम्य भावाः प्रजायन्ते तत्र चैवापियन्ति

padaccheda.iast: tat etat satyam yathā sudīptāt pāvakāt visphuliṅgāḥ sahasraśaḥ prabhavante sarūpāḥ tathā akṣarāt vividhāḥ somya bhāvāḥ prajāyante tatra ca eva apiyanti
padaccheda.deva: तत् एतत् सत्यम् यथा सुदीप्तात् पावकात् विस्फुलिङ्गाः सहस्रशः प्रभवन्ते सरूपाः तथा अक्षरात् विविधाः सोम्य भावाः प्रजायन्ते तत्र च एव अपियन्ति

translations.text: That is the truth: as from a blazing fire sparks of like form come forth by thousands, so, dear one, from the imperishable beings of many kinds (the jīvas) are born, and into it they return.

notes: Śaṅkara, introducing the khaṇḍa: all that the lower knowledge brings about has been told. The imperishable called Puruṣa, the true, from which as its root this round comes forth and into which it dissolves, and which being known all this is known, is the object of the higher knowledge of Brahman; that is now to be told.

Śaṅkara: the ‘truth’ of the lower knowledge, the fruit of rites, is true only relatively; this is the object of the higher knowledge, being the highest reality; the other is untrue, being the object of ignorance. Since the imperishable is wholly beyond the senses, an example is given so that it may be grasped as if perceived. Sparks, parts of the fire, come forth from a well-kindled fire in thousands, of the same nature as fire. bhāvāḥ: the jīvas, various because they follow the variety of bodies that are their adjuncts; as the spaces enclosed by pots and the like arise as the pots arise, so the jīvas are born as the bodily adjuncts made of name and form arise, and dissolve into the imperishable as those adjuncts dissolve, as the enclosed spaces when the pots are gone. As space is the cause of the rise and end of the enclosed spaces only through the pots, so the imperishable is the cause of the birth and end of the jīvas only through the bodily adjuncts made by name and form.

sanskrit.deva:
दिव्यो ह्यमूर्तः पुरुषः सबाह्याभ्यन्तरो ह्यजः ।
अप्राणो ह्यमनाः शुभ्रो ह्यक्षरात्परतः परः ॥ २ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
divyo hy amūrtaḥ puruṣaḥ sabāhyābhyantaro hy ajaḥ |
aprāṇo hy amanāḥ śubhro hy akṣarāt parataḥ paraḥ || 2 ||

lines.iast: divyo hy amūrtaḥ puruṣaḥ sabāhyābhyantaro hy ajaḥ
lines.deva: दिव्यो ह्यमूर्तः पुरुषः सबाह्याभ्यन्तरो ह्यजः

lines.iast: aprāṇo hy amanāḥ śubhro hy akṣarāt parataḥ paraḥ
lines.deva: अप्राणो ह्यमनाः शुभ्रो ह्यक्षरात्परतः परः

padaccheda.iast: divyaḥ hi amūrtaḥ puruṣaḥ sa-bāhya-abhyantaraḥ hi ajaḥ aprāṇaḥ hi amanāḥ śubhraḥ hi akṣarāt parataḥ paraḥ
padaccheda.deva: दिव्यः हि अमूर्तः पुरुषः स-बाह्य-अभ्यन्तरः हि अजः अप्राणः हि अमनाः शुभ्रः हि अक्षरात् परतः परः

words.meaning: with what is without and within

translations.text: For Puruṣa is self-luminous, formless, both without and within, unborn, without prāṇa, without mind, pure, higher than the high imperishable (the unmanifest).

notes: Śaṅkara, introducing the mantra: now it states the very nature of the imperishable, free of every distinction made by adjuncts, without any form, like space; described as ‘not this, not this’: higher than the imperishable called the unmanifest, the seed of name and form, which is high only with regard to its own effects.

Śaṅkara: divyaḥ: shining, being self-luminous; or dwelling in its own self; or not of the world. amūrtaḥ: without any form. puruṣaḥ: full, or lying in the city of the body. sabāhyābhyantaraḥ: together with what is outside and inside. ajaḥ: not born from anything, since there is nothing besides it to cause its birth, as wind causes bubbles on water, or pots the divisions of space. Since all changes have birth at their root, denying birth denies them all: so it is also ageless, deathless, imperishable, constant, fearless.

Śaṅkara, on aprāṇaḥ and amanāḥ: though, to those who see the differences of adjuncts, the body and the rest, it appears as having prāṇa, mind, senses and objects, as space appears to have a surface and dirt, to those who see its true nature it has no prāṇa, no moving air with its different powers of action, and no mind, made of intending and the rest, with its different powers of knowing. So all the breaths, the organs of action and their objects, intellect and mind, the organs of knowledge and their objects, are denied, as another text says, ‘it seems to think, it seems to move’ (Bṛhadāraṇyaka 4.3.7). Free of both kinds of adjunct, it is śubhra, pure. akṣarāt parataḥ paraḥ: ‘the imperishable’ is the unmanifest, marked by the adjunct of the seed of name and form, high because it is known as the seed of all effects and organs; higher than that high imperishable is Puruṣa without adjuncts, on which that imperishable, called space, is woven warp and woof.

Śaṅkara, on how it is without prāṇa: if prāṇa and the rest existed in their own nature before creation, as Puruṣa does, Puruṣa would have prāṇa through them; but they do not; so the supreme Puruṣa is without them, as Devadatta is sonless while his son is not yet born.

sanskrit.deva:
एतस्माज्जायते प्राणो मनः सर्वेन्द्रियाणि च ।
खं वायुर्ज्योतिरापः पृथिवी विश्वस्य धारिणी ॥ ३ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
etasmāj jāyate prāṇo manaḥ sarvendriyāṇi ca |
khaṃ vāyur jyotir āpaḥ pṛthivī viśvasya dhāriṇī || 3 ||

lines.iast: etasmāj jāyate prāṇo manaḥ sarvendriyāṇi ca
lines.deva: एतस्माज्जायते प्राणो मनः सर्वेन्द्रियाणि च

lines.iast: khaṃ vāyur jyotir āpaḥ pṛthivī viśvasya dhāriṇī
lines.deva: खं वायुर्ज्योतिरापः पृथिवी विश्वस्य धारिणी

padaccheda.iast: etasmāt jāyate prāṇaḥ manaḥ sarva-indriyāṇi ca kham vāyuḥ jyotiḥ āpaḥ pṛthivī viśvasya dhāriṇī
padaccheda.deva: एतस्मात् जायते प्राणः मनः सर्व-इन्द्रियाणि च खम् वायुः ज्योतिः आपः पृथिवी विश्वस्य धारिणी

translations.text: From him are born prāṇa, mind and all the senses; space, wind, fire, water, and the earth, the supporter of all.

notes: Śaṅkara: why prāṇa and the rest are not (in him): from this Puruṣa, marked by the adjunct of the seed of name and form, is born prāṇa, an object of ignorance, a modification, a mere name, untrue (‘a modification is a name, resting on speech’, Chāndogya 6.1.4). The supreme does not come to have prāṇa by a prāṇa that is untrue and an object of ignorance, any more than a sonless man has a son through a son seen in a dream. So also mind, all the senses and their objects are born from him; hence it is proved that he is truly, not figuratively, without prāṇa and the rest. As they are not in truth before they arise, so too when they have dissolved.

Śaṅkara: as the organs, so the elements, the causes of body and objects: kham, space; vāyu, the outer wind with its kinds, āvaha and the rest; jyotis, fire; āpaḥ, water; pṛthivī, the earth that bears all. These, with sound, touch, form, taste and smell, each having its own quality together with those of the ones before, are born from him.

sanskrit.deva:
अग्निर्मूर्धा चक्षुषी चन्द्रसूर्यौ दिशः श्रोत्रे वाग्विवृताश्च वेदाः ।
वायुः प्राणो हृदयं विश्वमस्य पद्भ्यां पृथिवी ह्येष सर्वभूतान्तरात्मा ॥ ४ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
agnir mūrdhā cakṣuṣī candrasūryau diśaḥ śrotre vāg vivṛtāś ca vedāḥ |
vāyuḥ prāṇo hṛdayaṃ viśvam asya padbhyāṃ pṛthivī hy eṣa sarvabhūtāntarātmā || 4 ||

lines.iast: agnir mūrdhā cakṣuṣī candrasūryau diśaḥ śrotre vāg vivṛtāś ca vedāḥ
lines.deva: अग्निर्मूर्धा चक्षुषी चन्द्रसूर्यौ दिशः श्रोत्रे वाग्विवृताश्च वेदाः

lines.iast: vāyuḥ prāṇo hṛdayaṃ viśvam asya padbhyāṃ pṛthivī hy eṣa sarvabhūtāntarātmā
lines.deva: वायुः प्राणो हृदयं विश्वमस्य पद्भ्यां पृथिवी ह्येष सर्वभूतान्तरात्मा

padaccheda.iast: agniḥ mūrdhā cakṣuṣī candra-sūryau diśaḥ śrotre vāk vivṛtāḥ ca vedāḥ vāyuḥ prāṇaḥ hṛdayam viśvam asya padbhyām pṛthivī hi eṣaḥ sarva-bhūta-antarātmā
padaccheda.deva: अग्निः मूर्धा चक्षुषी चन्द्र-सूर्यौ दिशः श्रोत्रे वाक् विवृताः च वेदाः वायुः प्राणः हृदयम् विश्वम् अस्य पद्भ्याम् पृथिवी हि एषः सर्व-भूत-अन्तरात्मा

grammar.en: past passive participle m. nom. pl.

words.meaning: the inner self of all beings

translations.text: Fire (heaven) is his head, the moon and the sun his eyes, the quarters his ears, the disclosed Vedas his speech, wind his prāṇa, the universe his heart; from his feet (came) the earth. He is the inner self of all beings.

notes: Śaṅkara, introducing the mantra: having stated briefly the imperishable, the true Puruṣa without qualities, the object of the higher knowledge, in ‘self-luminous, formless’ (2.1.2), the Upaniṣad goes on to state the same with qualities, at length; a thing told briefly and then at length is easily grasped, as in a sūtra and its commentary. Virāj, who is born within the egg from Hiraṇyagarbha, the first-born prāṇa, though known as other because other principles stand between, is also born from this Puruṣa and made of him: to show this the mantra describes him.

Śaṅkara: agni: the heavenly world (‘that world, Gautama, is a fire’, Chāndogya 5.4.1) is his head; the moon and the sun his eyes; ‘his’ is to be carried to each item. vāg vivṛtāś ca vedāḥ: his speech is the well-known Vedas, made manifest. hṛdayam: his inner organ is the whole world; for the world is only a modification of the inner organ, since it is seen to dissolve into the mind in deep sleep and in waking to spread out from it again like sparks from a fire. From his feet the earth was born. This god is Viṣṇu, the infinite, the first embodied one, whose body is the three worlds, the inner self of all beings: he it is who in all beings sees, hears, thinks and knows, the self of all the organs.

sanskrit.deva:
तस्मादग्निः समिधो यस्य सूर्यः सोमात्पर्जन्य ओषधयः पृथिव्याम् ।
पुमान्रेतः सिञ्चति योषितायां बह्वीः प्रजाः पुरुषात्संप्रसूताः ॥ ५ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
tasmād agniḥ samidho yasya sūryaḥ somāt parjanya oṣadhayaḥ pṛthivyām |
pumān retaḥ siñcati yoṣitāyāṃ bahvīḥ prajāḥ puruṣāt saṃprasūtāḥ || 5 ||

lines.iast: tasmād agniḥ samidho yasya sūryaḥ somāt parjanya oṣadhayaḥ pṛthivyām
lines.deva: तस्मादग्निः समिधो यस्य सूर्यः सोमात्पर्जन्य ओषधयः पृथिव्याम्

lines.iast: pumān retaḥ siñcati yoṣitāyāṃ bahvīḥ prajāḥ puruṣāt saṃprasūtāḥ
lines.deva: पुमान्रेतः सिञ्चति योषितायां बह्वीः प्रजाः पुरुषात्संप्रसूताः

padaccheda.iast: tasmāt agniḥ samidhaḥ yasya sūryaḥ somāt parjanyaḥ oṣadhayaḥ pṛthivyām pumān retaḥ siñcati yoṣitāyām bahvīḥ prajāḥ puruṣāt saṃprasūtāḥ
padaccheda.deva: तस्मात् अग्निः समिधः यस्य सूर्यः सोमात् पर्जन्यः ओषधयः पृथिव्याम् पुमान् रेतः सिञ्चति योषितायाम् बह्वीः प्रजाः पुरुषात् संप्रसूताः

grammar.en: past passive participle f. nom. pl.

translations.text: From him comes the fire (heaven) whose fuel is the sun; from soma (the moon) the rain-cloud; (from it) the plants on the earth; (from them) the man pours seed into the woman: so many creatures are born from Puruṣa.

notes: Śaṅkara, introducing the mantra: the creatures that go round by way of the five fires (Chāndogya 5.4–8) also are born from that Puruṣa.

Śaṅkara: from the supreme Puruṣa comes the fire that is a particular station of creatures, the heavenly world; its fuel is the sun, for the sun kindles heaven as fuel kindles fire. From the soma produced in that heavenly fire comes the rain-cloud, the second fire; from it the plants on the earth; from the plants, offered in the fire that is man and become his substance, the man-fire pours seed into the woman-fire. In this order many creatures, brāhmaṇas and the rest, are born from the supreme Puruṣa.

sanskrit.deva:
तस्मादृचः साम यजूंषि दीक्षा यज्ञाश्च सर्वे क्रतवो दक्षिणाश्च ।
संवत्सरश्च यजमानश्च लोकाः सोमो यत्र पवते यत्र सूर्यः ॥ ६ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
tasmād ṛcaḥ sāma yajūṃṣi dīkṣā yajñāś ca sarve kratavo dakṣiṇāś ca |
saṃvatsaraś ca yajamānaś ca lokāḥ somo yatra pavate yatra sūryaḥ || 6 ||

lines.iast: tasmād ṛcaḥ sāma yajūṃṣi dīkṣā yajñāś ca sarve kratavo dakṣiṇāś ca
lines.deva: तस्मादृचः साम यजूंषि दीक्षा यज्ञाश्च सर्वे क्रतवो दक्षिणाश्च

lines.iast: saṃvatsaraś ca yajamānaś ca lokāḥ somo yatra pavate yatra sūryaḥ
lines.deva: संवत्सरश्च यजमानश्च लोकाः सोमो यत्र पवते यत्र सूर्यः

padaccheda.iast: tasmāt ṛcaḥ sāma yajūṃṣi dīkṣā yajñāḥ ca sarve kratavaḥ dakṣiṇāḥ ca saṃvatsaraḥ ca yajamānaḥ ca lokāḥ somaḥ yatra pavate yatra sūryaḥ
padaccheda.deva: तस्मात् ऋचः साम यजूंषि दीक्षा यज्ञाः च सर्वे क्रतवः दक्षिणाः च संवत्सरः च यजमानः च लोकाः सोमः यत्र पवते यत्र सूर्यः

translations.text: From him come the verses, the chants and the formulas, consecration, all sacrifices and rites (with sacrificial posts), and the priests' fees; the year, the sacrificer, and the worlds where the moon purifies and where the sun (shines).

notes: Śaṅkara: the means of rites and their fruits also come from him. ṛcaḥ: mantras with a fixed number of syllables and feet, in metres such as the gāyatrī; sāma: sung with five or seven parts, with stobhas and the like; yajūṃṣi: in the form of prose, without fixed syllables or feet: so the mantras of three kinds. dīkṣā: the special observances of the agent, the muñja girdle and the rest. yajñāḥ: the agnihotra and the rest; kratavaḥ: those with a sacrificial post. dakṣiṇāḥ: from one cow up to one's whole property without limit. saṃvatsaraḥ: time, as a part of the rite; yajamānaḥ: the agent. lokāḥ: the worlds that are the fruit of his rites, where soma purifies the worlds and where the sun burns: reached by the two paths, of the southern and the northern course, the fruits of those without knowledge and of those with it.

sanskrit.deva:
तस्माच्च देवा बहुधा संप्रसूताः साध्या मनुष्याः पशवो वयांसि ।
प्राणापानौ व्रीहियवौ तपश्च श्रद्धा सत्यं ब्रह्मचर्यं विधिश्च ॥ ७ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
tasmāc ca devā bahudhā saṃprasūtāḥ sādhyā manuṣyāḥ paśavo vayāṃsi |
prāṇāpānau vrīhiyavau tapaś ca śraddhā satyaṃ brahmacaryaṃ vidhiś ca || 7 ||

lines.iast: tasmāc ca devā bahudhā saṃprasūtāḥ sādhyā manuṣyāḥ paśavo vayāṃsi
lines.deva: तस्माच्च देवा बहुधा संप्रसूताः साध्या मनुष्याः पशवो वयांसि

lines.iast: prāṇāpānau vrīhiyavau tapaś ca śraddhā satyaṃ brahmacaryaṃ vidhiś ca
lines.deva: प्राणापानौ व्रीहियवौ तपश्च श्रद्धा सत्यं ब्रह्मचर्यं विधिश्च

padaccheda.iast: tasmāt ca devāḥ bahudhā saṃprasūtāḥ sādhyāḥ manuṣyāḥ paśavaḥ vayāṃsi prāṇa-apānau vrīhi-yavau tapaḥ ca śraddhā satyam brahmacaryam vidhiḥ ca
padaccheda.deva: तस्मात् च देवाः बहुधा संप्रसूताः साध्याः मनुष्याः पशवः वयांसि प्राण-अपानौ व्रीहि-यवौ तपः च श्रद्धा सत्यम् ब्रह्मचर्यम् विधिः च

grammar.en: past passive participle m. nom. pl.

translations.text: From him are born the gods in their many kinds, the Sādhyas, men, cattle and birds; prāṇa and apāna, rice and barley; austerity, faith, truth, chastity and rule.

notes: Śaṅkara: the gods who have a part in the rites, in many groups, the Vasus and the rest; the Sādhyas, a class of gods; men, who are entitled to rites; cattle, of village and forest; birds. prāṇāpānau: the life of men and the rest; vrīhiyavau: rice and barley, for oblations. tapas: part of the rite, which refines the man, and also an independent means to its own fruit. śraddhā: the clearness of mind and conviction that comes before every effort toward a human end. satyam: avoiding falsehood, saying things as they are without causing pain. brahmacarya: abstaining from sexual union. vidhiḥ: the manner of doing.

sanskrit.deva:
सप्त प्राणाः प्रभवन्ति तस्मात्सप्तार्चिषः समिधः सप्त होमाः ।
सप्तेमे लोका येषु चरन्ति प्राणा गुहाशया निहिताः सप्त सप्त ॥ ८ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
sapta prāṇāḥ prabhavanti tasmāt saptārciṣaḥ samidhaḥ sapta homāḥ |
sapteme lokā yeṣu caranti prāṇā guhāśayā nihitāḥ sapta sapta || 8 ||

lines.iast: sapta prāṇāḥ prabhavanti tasmāt saptārciṣaḥ samidhaḥ sapta homāḥ
lines.deva: सप्त प्राणाः प्रभवन्ति तस्मात्सप्तार्चिषः समिधः सप्त होमाः

lines.iast: sapteme lokā yeṣu caranti prāṇā guhāśayā nihitāḥ sapta sapta
lines.deva: सप्तेमे लोका येषु चरन्ति प्राणा गुहाशया निहिताः सप्त सप्त

padaccheda.iast: sapta prāṇāḥ prabhavanti tasmāt sapta arciṣaḥ samidhaḥ sapta homāḥ sapta ime lokāḥ yeṣu caranti prāṇāḥ guhā-śayāḥ nihitāḥ sapta sapta
padaccheda.deva: सप्त प्राणाः प्रभवन्ति तस्मात् सप्त अर्चिषः समिधः सप्त होमाः सप्त इमे लोकाः येषु चरन्ति प्राणाः गुहा-शयाः निहिताः सप्त सप्त

grammar.en: past passive participle m. nom. pl.

translations.text: From him come forth the seven prāṇas (the senses of the head), their seven flames, seven fuels (their objects), seven offerings (their cognitions), and these seven worlds (their seats) in which the prāṇas move, lying in the cave, placed seven by seven (in each creature).

notes: Śaṅkara: sapta prāṇāḥ: the seven in the head. arciṣaḥ: their lights, each showing its own object. samidhaḥ: the seven objects, for the senses are kindled by objects. homāḥ: their cognitions of the objects (‘his knowing is what he offers’, Taittirīya Nārāyaṇa 80). lokāḥ: the seats of the senses, in which the prāṇas move; this qualifies the prāṇas, to show that prāṇa, apāna and the other breaths are not meant. guhāśayāḥ: lying in the cave, the body or the heart, in sleep. nihitāḥ: set by the creator, seven by seven, in each creature.

Śaṅkara, summing up: the rites of the knowing, who sacrifice to the Self, with their fruits, and the rites of the unknowing, with their means and fruits, all come forth from the supreme, all-knowing Puruṣa: that is the sense of the section.

sanskrit.deva:
अतः समुद्रा गिरयश्च सर्वेऽस्मात्स्यन्दन्ते सिन्धवः सर्वरूपाः ।
अतश्च सर्वा ओषधयो रसश्च येनैष भूतैस्तिष्ठते ह्यन्तरात्मा ॥ ९ ॥
sanskrit.iast:
ataḥ samudrā girayaś ca sarve 'smāt syandante sindhavaḥ sarvarūpāḥ |
ataś ca sarvā oṣadhayo rasaś ca yenaiṣa bhūtais tiṣṭhate hy antarātmā || 9 ||

lines.iast: ataḥ samudrā girayaś ca sarve 'smāt syandante sindhavaḥ sarvarūpāḥ
lines.deva: अतः समुद्रा गिरयश्च सर्वेऽस्मात्स्यन्दन्ते सिन्धवः सर्वरूपाः

lines.iast: ataś ca sarvā oṣadhayo rasaś ca yenaiṣa bhūtais tiṣṭhate hy antarātmā
lines.deva: अतश्च सर्वा ओषधयो रसश्च येनैष भूतैस्तिष्ठते ह्यन्तरात्मा

padaccheda.iast: ataḥ samudrāḥ girayaḥ ca sarve asmāt syandante sindhavaḥ sarva-rūpāḥ ataḥ ca sarvāḥ oṣadhayaḥ rasaḥ ca yena eṣaḥ bhūtaiḥ tiṣṭhate hi antarātmā
padaccheda.deva: अतः समुद्राः गिरयः च सर्वे अस्मात् स्यन्दन्ते सिन्धवः सर्व-रूपाः अतः च सर्वाः ओषधयः रसः च येन एषः भूतैः तिष्ठते हि अन्तरात्मा

translations.text: From him come all the seas and the mountains; from him flow the rivers of every form; from him come all plants and savour, by which this inner self (the subtle body) stands, surrounded by the elements.

notes: Śaṅkara: the seas, salt and the rest; the mountains, Himavat and the rest; the rivers, Gaṅgā and the rest, of many forms; the plants, rice, barley and the rest; and savour of six kinds, sweet and the rest, by which the inner self stands surrounded by the five gross elements. antarātmā: the subtle body, so called because it stands between the body and the Self, like a self.

sanskrit.deva:
पुरुष एवेदं विश्वं कर्म तपो ब्रह्म परामृतम् ।
एतद्यो वेद निहितं गुहायां सोऽविद्याग्रन्थिं विकिरतीह सोम्य ॥ १० ॥
sanskrit.iast:
puruṣa evedaṃ viśvaṃ karma tapo brahma parāmṛtam |
etad yo veda nihitaṃ guhāyāṃ so 'vidyāgranthiṃ vikiratīha somya || 10 ||

lines.iast: puruṣa evedaṃ viśvaṃ karma tapo brahma parāmṛtam
lines.deva: पुरुष एवेदं विश्वं कर्म तपो ब्रह्म परामृतम्

lines.iast: etad yo veda nihitaṃ guhāyāṃ so 'vidyāgranthiṃ vikiratīha somya
lines.deva: एतद्यो वेद निहितं गुहायां सोऽविद्याग्रन्थिं विकिरतीह सोम्य

padaccheda.iast: puruṣaḥ eva idam viśvam karma tapaḥ brahma parāmṛtam etat yaḥ veda nihitam guhāyām saḥ avidyā-granthim vikirati iha somya
padaccheda.deva: पुरुषः एव इदम् विश्वम् कर्म तपः ब्रह्म परामृतम् एतत् यः वेद निहितम् गुहायाम् सः अविद्या-ग्रन्थिम् विकिरति इह सोम्य

grammar.en: past passive participle n. acc. sg.

translations.text: Puruṣa alone is this universe: action and austerity (knowledge and its fruit); Brahman, the supreme and immortal. He who knows this set in the cave (of the heart) scatters here (while living), dear one, the knot of ignorance.

notes: Śaṅkara: since all this is born from Puruṣa, the modification is a name resting on speech, untrue; ‘Puruṣa’ alone is true; so Puruṣa alone is this universe, and there is no universe other than Puruṣa. This answers the question ‘what is it which being known, all this becomes known?’ (1.1.3): when this supreme Self, Puruṣa, the cause of all, is known, it is known that Puruṣa alone is this universe and nothing else is. What is this universe? Action, the agnihotra and the rest; tapas, knowledge; and the fruit made by them: all this is the effect of Brahman. He who knows ‘therefore all is Brahman, the supreme immortal, and I am that’, set in the cave, the heart, of all beings, by that knowing scatters, destroys, the knot of ignorance, the impressions of ignorance hardened like a knot, here, while living, not after death. somya: you who are pleasing to see.
